source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Setup the system to a standard supported configuration.
2. Boot to OS.
3. Remove the Heat sink or Use a Peltier Device to slowly heat the CPU indicated under Configurations to the TWarning Threshold (Monitor the temperature increase via BMC web interface)
4. Once TWarning Threshold is reached, slowly proceed to add heat until TCritical threshold is reached.   (NOTE:  If you go too fast you may only trip the TCritical Threshold)
5. Continue Heating until system resets

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. System will shutdown once TCritical Threshold has been reached
2. BMC error log will show an over-temperature condition has been detected on CPUx
3. Temperature LED will light if there is one on the Diagnostic Panel
4. If there is a LCD Panel (Aria),  CPU Over Temp error information will be displayed with details of affected CPU
5. Corresponding CPU lightpath will light
6. Front Panel Fault Light will Light
7. Once all checks are complete in during run time, reboot the system and check the uEFI SEL to ensure the corresponding log for CPU Over Temp was logged properly as well as the system reseta

original_test_intent: Drive one identified CPU through Project-defined TWarning and TCritical protection, verify its BMC and UEFI events plus applicable temperature/LCD/lightpath/front-panel indicators, and prove the specified protective power action and safe recovery. The source disagrees whether the terminal action is reset or shutdown.
original_method: Boot the OS, remove the CPU heatsink or use a Peltier device, watch BMC temperature, ramp through TWarning and TCritical, continue heating until reset, then inspect indicators and logs. Criteria instead say shutdown at TCritical followed by a later reboot, so the stopping and recovery sequence is not authoritative.
manual_activity: Only after correction, a qualified thermal engineer installs and operates the approved fixture, independently observes temperatures and every applicable physical indicator, controls the hard abort and cooling restoration, and inspects the CPU/cooling assembly. Automation may collect read-only synchronized telemetry and logs.
required_inputs: Engineer-approved terminal action at each threshold: warning only, orderly shutdown, hardware power removal or reset, including timing/tolerance and allowed post-trip reboot
Exact CPU/socket and authoritative sensor identity, units, TWarning/TCritical/hysteresis/tolerance, maximum safe boundary and expected assert/deassert events
Vendor-approved calibrated thermal stimulus; fixture/adapter contact method, independent probe locations, ramp rate, dwell and sensor-lag allowance
Hardwired over-temperature/power cutoff independent of BMC/host software, emergency cooling, attended abort owner and interlock validation
Applicability and Expected Values for BMC/UEFI SEL, diagnostic temperature LED, Aria LCD, CPU lightpath and front-panel fault light
Dedicated SUT, quiesced data, OOB/serial monitoring, post-trip cooldown, heatsink/TIM/torque restoration if disturbed, inspection and recovery plan
safety_requirements: Do not remove or loosen a heatsink on an energized CPU and do not continue heating until an unspecified reset; the original wording is preserved as a hazardous source method, not an executable recommendation.
Do not substitute 25 warm reboots or read-only temperature observation for the required thermal warning/critical protection path.
Use an approved interlocked fixture with a calibrated independent probe and a hard cutoff that does not depend on BMC WebUI update rate, host software or the protection path under test.

Set ramp, dwell, absolute temperature, time-at-temperature and sensor-disagreement abort limits below the vendor damage boundary; stop immediately on loss of cooling, implausible telemetry, unexpected action or missed protection.
Export logs before any approved clear; preserve the first trip and never repeat or automatically reboot after an unexpected result.

After protection, remove heat and keep restart inhibited until independent and BMC temperatures are within the approved recovery range, cooling is correctly installed and hardware/power rails are inspected.
Restore cooling assembly and settings, verify sensor plausibility, boot only with engineer approval, run hardware/host health checks and preserve all trip/recovery evidence.
agent_execution_scope: Before correction, perform no DUT, thermal, cooling, reboot or log-clear action and record only the unresolved safety and terminal-action semantics.
After approval, collect synchronized BMC sensor/threshold/event, independent fixture/probe, host power/state, fan, BMC/UEFI SEL and recovery telemetry around engineer-controlled heating.
Organize engineer-captured physical LED/LCD/lightpath evidence by applicability and timestamp; report TWarning, TCritical, terminal action and recovery as separate checkpoints.
Do not apply heat, manipulate cooling, control power, infer thresholds, claim visual observations, retry, reboot after trip or issue DUT verdicts.
engineer_actions: Correct reset versus shutdown and post-trip reboot semantics in the Review layer while preserving Master, and approve the complete threshold/event/indicator matrix.
Approve and operate the calibrated interlocked fixture, independent sensing, ramp/dwell/abort/cooldown and emergency recovery; supervise all physical observations.
Inspect and restore cooling/hardware, authorize any reboot and issue per-checkpoint plus final DUT verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Warm Reboot 25 times belongs to row 1527 and provides zero TWarning, TCritical, protection or indicator coverage; its plaintext credential and disabled host-key patterns are rejected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No stimulus command until engineers correct the terminal action and approve a hardware-interlocked thermal SOP. Thereafter use only read-only telemetry collection around the attended physical fixture.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The heatsink/Peltier choices, TWarning then TCritical ramp, continue-until-reset wording, shutdown criterion, all conditional indicators, UEFI SEL, no Script and 10/5-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.status: ENGINEER DECISION AND SAFE METHOD PENDING
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Define the terminal action and full threshold/event matrix; use a calibrated local thermal fixture with independent sensing and hardware cutoff; ramp and dwell within approved limits; capture warning, critical, protection and indicators; hard-stop, cool, inspect, restore and only then authorize recovery.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact CPU/socket/cooling design, BMC sensor model and front-panel/Aria option population.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record CPU stepping, board, BIOS/BMC/CPLD, sensor/SDR, fixture/controller firmware and calibration identifiers.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: CPU/platform thermal qualification limits, protection behavior, sensor/event and indicator mapping, cooling assembly and fixture safety procedures.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Does not overwrite Master; it replaces the executable recommendation for uncontrolled heatsink removal/heat-until-reset with an engineer-approved bounded interlocked method and separates shutdown, reset and reboot checkpoints.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A simulated threshold injection can validate BMC events and indicators but cannot by itself prove the physical CPU thermal protection path; any alternative stimulus must state which sensor, silicon protection and indicator coverage is equivalent or absent.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Terminal-action decision, thresholds/events, interlocked fixture, independent sensing, indicators and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: BMC telemetry can lag a rapid local junction rise, so software monitoring alone cannot prevent thermal overshoot or permanent damage.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may select an approved chamber, thermal head, Peltier fixture or staged injection, but must retain the original physical-heating objective, document stimulus equivalence and explicitly disclose any CPU silicon, sensor, protection-action or physical-indicator path not exercised.
expected_evidence: Preserved source/duplicate conflict plus dated engineer decision for shutdown versus reset, post-trip reboot and safe stimulus
CPU/socket/sensor identity; threshold/hysteresis/tolerance, event and applicable indicator matrix; platform and firmware versions
Fixture/probe calibration, placement, hard-interlock proof, ramp/dwell/absolute/time aborts, emergency cooling and attended authorization
Synchronized independent and BMC temperature ramp showing TWarning and TCritical checkpoints, fan/power/host state and first-trip timing
BMC error/SEL, UEFI SEL and applicable diagnostic LED, Aria LCD, CPU lightpath and front-panel fault evidence tied to CPUx
Protection action, hard-stop/cooldown, restored cooling/TIM/torque if applicable, hardware/sensor/host recovery checks and engineer verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure says to continue heating until the system resets, while Criterion 1 says the system shuts down at TCritical and Criterion 7 then instructs a later reboot; reset, shutdown and operator reboot are distinct terminal actions and stop conditions. The code is also reused at row 1527 and DeepSeek imports that unrelated warm-reboot method.

blocked_analysis.analysis: This is not only missing threshold values. The source's terminal protection action conflicts, and its stated powered-heatsink-removal/unbounded heat-until-reset methods lack a safe stopping condition. Executing before engineer correction could damage hardware and still yield an unauthoritative verdict.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects warm-reboot substitution and unsafe credential handling as unrelated to thermal protection.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on BLOCKED and retains the interlocked-fixture requirement while making the reset/shutdown/reboot contradiction an explicit engineer decision.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces PARTIAL command review with the actual hazardous thermal and indicator acceptance boundary.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Keeps the safe-method block but adds an independent hard cutoff, sensor-lag analysis, precise terminal-action checkpoints and post-trip restart inhibition.

review_improvement: Prevents uncontrolled CPU heating and a false warm-reboot result while preserving warning, critical, physical indicator, SEL and real protection coverage for a safely engineered method.
independent_technical_reasoning: A local CPU junction can heat faster than BMC polling reports, so heatsink removal or open-loop heating has no reliable software abort. Separately, shutdown, watchdog-like reset and later operator reboot produce different evidence and recovery states. Until engineers define the expected terminal action and a hard-interlocked stimulus, the original functional objective must remain intact but execution must be blocked.
